Images are tokenized based on their pixel dimensions using the following formula:
A 1024×768 image would consume: (1024 × 768) / 750 = 1,048 tokens

The search_domain_filter parameter accepts a list of domain strings:
Allowlist (no prefix): Include only results from these domains. ["reuters.com", "apnews.com"] means search only Reuters and AP News.

Never mix allowlist and denylist entries in the same request.
The API does not support combining "reuters.com" and "-reddit.com" in the same array.
Use either all allowlist or all denylist entries.

How Structured Outputs Work
output_text

The schema format follows JSON Schema with a few constraints specific to the Perplexity API:
No recursive schemas.
The schema cannot reference itself.
object
No unconstrained objects.
Avoid additionalProperties: true or bare object types without defined properties.
name
Named schemas required.
Each schema needs a name field for identification.

Schema Design Constraints
The Agent API enforces these constraints on JSON schemas:
additionalProperties
false
additionalProperties must be false.
Every "type": "object" in the schema must include "additionalProperties": false.
This applies to the top-level schema and all nested objects.
A schema cannot reference itself with $ref pointing to its own definition.
properties
No unconstrained dicts.
Avoid "type": "object" without properties.
Every object type must have explicitly defined properties.
required
All properties should be required.
While optional properties are allowed, making all properties required ensures consistent output structure.
No $ref to external schemas.
All definitions must be inline.

Get web-grounded answers with built-in citations in one call, or access third-party models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and xAI with …

Fetch Markdown, HTML, links, highlights, and metadata from URLs you already have, and score each page with yes or no …

Run web searches or page checks on a schedule and read the saved results.

Saved state
The monitor keeps saved state between runs.
Later runs use this saved state to find what is new.
The next run is a first check when one of these values differs from the saved state:
The task in input
The top-level goal
The profile id or version
The freshness filter
The domains in either domain list
An equivalent value does not reset the saved state.
For example, the order of the values in a list has no effect.

Run failures
A run fails with error.code: "source_failed" in conditions such as these:
The effort version does not exist.
The Agent API cannot find or access the profile.
The agent cannot retrieve information that is relevant to the task.
The service cannot read the answer from the agent.
error.code
error.message

Use error.code in your application logic.
Read error.message for the reason.
Do not parse error.message.
After three source failures without a successful run between them, the service pauses the monitor automatically.

Verify signatures
Webhook deliveries use Standard Webhooks v1.
They include three headers.
Verify the signature before you process the event:
webhook-id
The ID of the delivery.
The ID stays the same for all retries of that delivery.
webhook-timestamp
The time in Unix seconds when the service signs the attempt.
webhook-signature
One or more entries.
A space separates each pair of entries.
Each entry starts with v1,, then has a base64 signature.
In this notation, and are the values from the request headers.
The + joins the bytes.
signing_key
signed_payload
Use signing_key to calculate the HMAC-SHA256 of signed_payload.
Encode the digest in base64.
Compare the result with the v1 signatures from the header in constant time.
Accept a signature that matches only if the timestamp is within five minutes of your clock.
Use the original bytes of the request body before you parse or reserialize the JSON.
Use webhook-id to remove duplicate events.

Delivery and retries
Return any 2xx response within 10 seconds.
Then process the event asynchronously.
The service ignores the response body.
It does not follow redirects.
Timeout, network error, 408, 429, or 5xx
The service retries after 5 seconds, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, 5 hours, and 10 hours.
It makes seven attempts over about 17.6 hours.
3xx, 410, other 4xx, or TLS certificate failure
The service ends the delivery without another attempt.
Delivery errors do not change the status of a completed run.
If delivery fails repeatedly, the service can automatically pause the monitor.
